points.quote: The permitted use of AI for a particular assessment or learning activity should be explicitly outlined by Module Coordinators or Supervisors and may differ between modules or contexts according to the University of Stirling’s AI Assessment Scale.
points.gist: Module Coordinators or Supervisors should explicitly state what AI use is permitted, which can differ between modules under the AI Assessment Scale.

points.quote: Submission of any form of assessment, which the student has not individually created or written, as the content wholly or substantially originates from output of an artificial intelligence tool.
points.anchor: 21.1.2. Inappropriate use of artificial intelligence tools
points.gist: Submitting an assessment that wholly or substantially originates from AI output, not individually created by the student, is listed as inappropriate AI use.

points.quote: When part of an assessment originates from an artificial tool without appropriate acknowledgement.
points.anchor: 21.1.2. Inappropriate use of artificial intelligence tools
points.gist: Using an AI tool for part of an assessment without appropriate acknowledgement is inappropriate use.

points.quote: Where an artificial intelligence tool has been used in a manner contrary to the instructions of the particular assessment.
points.anchor: 21.1.2. Inappropriate use of artificial intelligence tools
points.gist: Using an AI tool contrary to the instructions of the particular assessment is inappropriate use.

points.quote: Making false or misleading statements as to the extent to which, and how, artificial intelligence tools were used in an assessment.
points.gist: False or misleading statements about the extent and manner of AI use in an assessment are a form of academic misconduct.

points.quote: Unauthorised notes or information resources in any form, including AI tools.
points.gist: Unauthorised notes or information resources, including AI tools, are unacceptable during an assessment under exam conditions.

points.quote: It is noted that the use of AI tools to paraphrase other students’ work is strictly prohibited as it constitutes a case of collusion.
points.gist: Using AI tools to paraphrase other students’ work is strictly prohibited and counts as collusion.

points.quote: such a use of AI proofreading tools beyond assistive purposes is also prohibited, unless tasks allow their use for the purposes of formation of ideas or concepts.
points.gist: Using AI proofreading tools beyond assistive purposes is prohibited unless the task allows their use for forming ideas or concepts.

points.quote: Secure and always protect their work, including from unsolicited capture for AI training purposes by online AI providers.
points.gist: Students are to secure and protect their work, including from unsolicited capture for AI training by online AI providers.

points.quote: use of most external AI tools for rephrasing students’ own material to avoid selfplagiarism entails the risk of student's own work being used to train future generations of AI services
points.gist: Using most external AI tools to rephrase your own material risks that work being used to train future AI services.

points.quote: Students are still required to use AI appropriately according to the University Policy on the use of AI, and to adhere to standards of academic integrity; this includes transparent acknowledgement of AI used.
points.gist: Students with approved adjustments allowing specific AI functionalities must still use AI appropriately and transparently acknowledge AI used.

points.quote: Users should be aware of the current technical limitations of AI, including but not limited to: generation of inaccurate or fabricated information, lack of source transparency, and reproduction of unintended and potentially harmful biases embedded in training data.
points.gist: Users should know AI can generate inaccurate or fabricated information, lacks source transparency and reproduces biases from training data.

points.quote: Inappropriate quoting from sources, including artificial intelligence tools, whether or not referenced in-text and/or in the bibliography
points.gist: Inappropriate quoting from sources, including AI tools, is poor academic practice whether or not referenced.
